ai.title: Add conversation progress detection and refine system prompts
ai.summary: New `backend/src/conversation-progress.ts` introduces `checkConversationProgress` (Claude Sonnet) and `checkToAllowUnboundedIteration` (GPT-4o Mini) to detect loops and unbounded requests. `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` integrates these checks to pause or continue based on progress, replacing simple message-count limits with semantic evaluation. `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` removes the `checkFiles` option from `getAgentSystemPrompt` and adds explicit instructions to avoid global package installs and use project-specific package managers. `backend/knowledge.md` documents the new WebSocket flow and conversation management architecture.

eli5.text: The assistant now watches conversations more intelligently to avoid getting stuck in circles or running forever. Instead of just counting messages, it checks whether the task seems complete or the conversation has gone quiet, then decides to pause or keep working. You, as the person watching the assistant work, would notice it stopping sooner when progress stalls instead of looping endlessly. This makes sessions more efficient and prevents wasted effort, though the core interaction of asking and editing remains unchanged.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.113
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.113 in `npm-app/package.json`. Internal release marker.

eli5.text: The assistant now watches whether each answer is actually making progress against your request, and when it notices a stall, it adjusts how it talks to keep things moving forward. If you've ever gotten an answer that seemed to repeat itself or stop short, the new version is set to recognize that pattern and continue in a more useful direction. A few related stability fixes are also included for anyone updating to this release.

ai.title: Add changesAlreadyApplied to websocket debug log
ai.summary: The `response-complete` debug log in `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts` now includes the `changesAlreadyApplied` object. This provides visibility into idempotency state during websocket action processing. Scope limited to backend websocket logging.

eli5.text: The server now writes a bit more information into its technical logs. When your request finishes being processed over the connection, the log that used to list only the response, changes, and tool calls now also lists the idempotency state object. This gives backend engineers better visibility when troubleshooting duplicate request handling, but does not change anything you experience. The change is live today across the backend logging system.

ai.title: Prevent empty blocks in file version and project prompts
ai.summary: Added filters to remove empty strings from prompt construction in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. Prevents empty blocks in `getFileVersionUpdates` and `getProjectFilesPromptContent` when file lists are empty. Ensures cleaner prompt output by excluding empty file version arrays and project file strings.

eli5.text: When the assistant builds its instructions about your files, it used to include empty sections if there were no files to show, leaving gaps in the prompt. Now it quietly skips those empty sections so the instructions read cleanly. You wouldn't see this yourself, but the assistant's behind-the-scenes reasoning will be tidier.

ai.title: Revert Continue-until-condition logic
ai.summary: Reverts 'Continue until user condition' feature. Removes `conversation-progress.ts` and associated logic from `main-prompt.ts` and `system-prompt.ts`. Eliminates GPT-4 Mini/Claude Sonnet checks for loop detection and unbounded iteration permissions. Restores simpler pause mechanism based on message count in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant used to keep going and automatically decide when to stop based on checking your conversation with it, but that system has been turned off. Now the assistant relies on a simpler approach: it counts messages and stops after a set amount rather than analyzing whether the task is done. If you were using the assistant and noticed it no longer seemed to adapt its behavior based on conversation progress or model checks, that feature is no longer active, and any tools or prompts that depended on it have been removed.

ai.title: Re-enable conversation progress checks and unbounded iteration logic
ai.summary: Reverts previous revert, restoring `conversation-progress.ts` to handle smart continuation. Implements `checkConversationProgress` using Claude Sonnet to detect loops or satisfied requests, and `checkToAllowUnboundedIteration` using GPT-4 Mini to identify user intent for 'do all' tasks. Updates `main-prompt.ts` to pause only when appropriate, replacing rigid message counts with dynamic progress evaluation. Refines `system-prompt.ts` to remove `checkFiles` option and enforce local package installation via project-specific managers.

eli5.text: The coding assistant can now better decide whether it has finished what you asked or is stuck repeating itself, instead of blindly running a fixed number of steps. When you give a broad 'do everything' instruction, it checks your intent first and lets the task run longer when that's genuinely what you wanted. If you look at an ongoing session, you'll see it pause for your input only when it makes sense, rather than stopping on a rigid schedule. The assistant must also install any new tools into your own project folder, not somewhere shared on your computer.

ai.title: Remove STOPMARKER cleanup and empty file filter
ai.summary: Removed `fullResponse.replace(STOP_MARKER, '')` from `main-prompt.ts` and `.filter((str) => str)` from `system-prompt.ts`. These changes eliminate post-processing that stripped stop markers and filtered empty strings, likely relying on upstream handling or simplifying logic. Scope limited to `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. The `STOP_MARKER` is no longer explicitly removed from the response string in the stop condition.

eli5.text: The assistant used to quietly clean up two small artifacts in its output: a special end-of-message marker that was being stripped out, and blank lines that were being removed. Those cleanup steps have been turned off, so the message text now reaches you exactly as the assistant generates it, without the extra post-processing. Whoever receives these messages will see them with one fewer pass of editing applied behind the scenes.

ai.title: System prompt: terminal checks now opt-in via knowledge files
ai.summary: Updated backend/src/system-prompt.ts to change verification behavior. The prompt now instructs the agent to check knowledge files for verification protocols and to skip terminal commands if none are specified. This removes the previous default behavior of running tests/linters/type-checkers after every edit.

eli5.text: The AI coding assistant will no longer automatically run tests, linters, or type-checkers after making every edit unless a specific project file explicitly asks it to. Instead, it now looks for instructions in files like knowledge.md to determine whether and what checks to run. If no such instructions exist in the project, it skips the checks entirely rather than running default commands. This change is already live, making the assistant quieter and less likely to interrupt your workflow with automatic validation unless your project settings call for it.

ai.title: Add where to SKIPPEDTERMINALCOMMANDS
ai.summary: Added 'where' to the SKIPPED_TERMINAL_COMMANDS list in common/src/constants.ts. This prevents Freebuff from attempting to execute the 'where' command during agent runs, aligning it with other skipped utilities like 'which' and 'who'. Scope is limited to the core constants module.

eli5.text: The system now skips running a utility called 'where' while it works through tasks, just like it already skips similar system commands. This only matters if you let the system run automated tasks for you; you don't need to do anything differently. The change is already in place and takes effect right away, no restart or setting to flip.
